trust_boundaries: Auth Layer to Redis Data Zone
architecture_summary.operational_context: Cloud-hosted, internet-facing multi-tier REST API with API gateway, authentication service, Redis session cache, and application server.

threat_actors.name: External opportunistic attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Credential theft, data exfiltration, and API abuse for financial gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Internet-facing API endpoints, credential stuffing, and exploitation of public-facing gateway vulnerabilities
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud infrastructure
No pre-existing insider knowledge or valid internal credentials
No direct network access to Redis or App Server from the internet
Cannot bypass enforced TLS without a privileged network position

threat_actors.name: Malicious insider
threat_actors.motivation: Data exfiltration, fraud, or sabotage using authorized access
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Valid API credentials or operator access to Auth Service or App Server
non_capabilities: No physical access to cloud provider facilities
Cannot unilaterally modify gateway or auth code without change approval
No direct internet exposure of Redis
Limited to granted IAM roles and API scopes
Cannot disable organization-wide logging without detection

attack_paths.impact: Account takeover and unauthorized API access to confidential data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Internet-facing authentication endpoint with password-based login and no confirmed universal MFA makes automated credential stuffing feasible.

attack_paths.impact: Gateway compromise, authentication bypass, or pivot into internal service network
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Gateway is internet-facing but patched and fronted by a WAF; exploit requires a new vulnerability or misconfiguration.

attack_paths.impact: Theft of bearer tokens or credentials in transit
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: TLS is enforced, but clients on untrusted networks remain exposed to misconfiguration or downgrade attacks.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Auth Service host or internal Auth-to-Redis network segment
attack_paths.impact: Session token theft enabling impersonation of authenticated users
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Redis stores session material and may be reachable from a compromised Auth Service; authentication and segmentation reduce but do not eliminate exposure.

attack_paths.entry_point: API Gateway route using a valid but over-privileged token
attack_paths.impact: Unauthorized read access to application data and business logic
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Stolen or over-scoped tokens can reach App Server through the gateway; token scoping and least privilege are only partially implemented.

mitigations.control_name: Rate limiting and account lockout for authentication endpoints
Multi-factor authentication for privileged and API access
Establish and maintain a vulnerability management process
Data-in-transit protection with TLS and HSTS
Least privilege and token scoping for App Server access

findings.severity_rationale: Credential stuffing can yield valid sessions and confidential API data, but partial MFA and rate limiting reduce exploitability.
A gateway exploit would bypass a primary trust boundary and expose internal services, though WAF and patching lower likelihood.
TLS is enforced, so interception requires a privileged network position or misconfiguration; impact is credential or session theft.
Redis holds session material and is reachable from the auth zone; theft enables impersonation but segmentation limits reach.
Valid but over-scoped tokens can read application data through the gateway; least privilege is only partially enforced.
